title: Confidence Calibration and Annotator-Anchoring Feedback Loop Protocol
author: Sofia Kwan
content:
Overview

This document defines the Confidence Calibration and Annotator-Anchoring Feedback Loop Protocol (the "protocol") for Redwood Inference evaluation pipelines. The protocol standardizes how model-assigned confidence scores are calibrated, how annotator reference anchors are created and maintained, and how automated relabel/recalibration triggers propagate into the eval-harness and production monitoring. The goal is to keep measured quality aligned with customer-facing uncertainty estimates and enable automated, auditable adjustments to evaluation labels and thresholds.

Audience
- Applied ML engineers
- Evaluator/operators
- QA and annotation leads
- Model onboarding owners

Motivation
- Models often report uncalibrated logits that misrepresent real-world correctness probabilities, causing mis-routed fallbacks and incorrect SLO decisions.
- Annotator judgments drift over time; we need conservative anchoring to maintain consistent ground truth while allowing controlled updates.
- Automated relabeling with poor controls can silently degrade eval quality; the protocol enforces checks, telemetry gates, and human review windows.

Key definitions
- Confidence score: normalized [0,1] probability output attached to a response or label.
- Anchor set: a curated subset of labeled examples used as stable reference for annotator decisions.
- Calibration transform: the mapping applied to raw model scores (e.g., temperature scaling, isotonic regression).
- Recalibration window: a time-bounded batch of data used for recalibration; default = 7 days.

High-level flow
1) Ingest: live/prod-sampled telemetry routed into the eval-harness with metadata (route, model_version, prompt_shard, token_count, response_id).
2) Score bucketing: responses bucketed into deciles of raw score and further stratified by slice (language, length, intent).
3) Anchor sampling: select per-slice anchor candidates (see Anchor selection rules).
4) Annotate & adjudicate: anchors are double-annotated and adjudicated; results persist to the anchor registry.
5) Calibration fit: for each model_version+slice, fit candidate calibration transforms and compute calibration metrics (ECE, Brier, calibration curves).
6) Gate & deploy: if transforms improve ECE by >= 15% and do not reduce recall on safety sentinel slices by > 1%, they are promoted following the Rollout policy.
7) Continuous monitoring: live checks compare predicted confidence vs. anchor-derived empirical frequency; drift beyond thresholds triggers a recalibration investigation ticket.

Anchor selection rules
- Size: target 2k examples per major slice (language x intent), minimum 250 for low-volume slices.
- Staleness: anchors older than 90 days must be reviewed before use.
- Diversity: anchors must cover top 10 tokens length deciles and include at least 10% adversarially generated probes.
- Ownership: each anchor set has an owner (applied-ml engineer or annotation lead).

Calibration methods and recommended defaults
- Temperature scaling (TS): fast baseline; recommended first-step.
- Isotonic regression (IR): non-parametric; use when TS residuals are large and sample size > 1000.
- Platt scaling: logistic variant for binary-convertible tasks.
- Dirichlet calibration: for multi-class probability vectors where class-count > 5.
- Ensemble calibration: blend transforms across time windows for smoother behavior.

Recommended default pipeline (YAML example)
config: |
  pipeline:
    sample_rate: 0.01  # 1% production sampling or min 5000/day
    recalibration_window: 7d
    calibration_methods: ["temperature_scaling","isotonic_regression"]
    anchor_target_per_slice: 2000
    ece_improvement_threshold: 0.15
    safety_recall_drop_threshold: 0.01
  outputs:
    promoted_transform_registry: "/eval/calibration/transforms"
    anchor_registry: "/eval/anchors"

Metrics and thresholds
- ECE (expected calibration error): primary metric. Target: ECE <= 0.03 for high-volume slices, <= 0.06 for low-volume.
- Brier score: auxiliary check for probabilistic fidelity.
- Reliability diagrams: visual artifacts retained for 180 days.
- Anchor stability index (ASI): fraction of anchor labels unchanged after re-annotation; target > 0.92.
- Drift signal: 3-sigma deviation in predicted vs empirical frequencies across three consecutive windows triggers investigation.

Rollout policy (promotion steps)
1) Dry-run: candidate transform applied to a 0% production dry-run traffic but evaluated in the eval-harness; compare metrics.
2) Shadow deploy: apply transform within shadow-routing path for 2–3 days; measure downstream decision differences.
3) Canary: route 1–5% real traffic; require metric checks to hold for 48h.
4) Gradual ramp: 5→25→100% over 24–72h with automatic abort on metric regression.

Human-in-the-loop and automated relabeling
- Automated relabeling allowed only if all of: anchor ASI >= 0.95, model_version stable for 14+ days, and adjudicated sample passes QA audit.
- When automated relabel occurs, create audit entry: {response_id, old_label, new_label, reason, evidence_anchor_ids, operator}.
- All automated relabels appear for 7 days in the annotation review queue for spot checks.

CLI examples
- Export candidate anchors for a slice:
  rdl eval export-anchors --model v2.3 --slice "en+intent:faq" --out anchors.csv
- Fit temperature scaling on anchors:
  rdl eval fit-calibration --method temperature --anchors anchors.csv --out transform_v2.3_ts.json
- Simulate promotion impact:
  rdl eval simulate-promotion --transform transform_v2.3_ts.json --metrics ece,brier --window 7d

Operational runbook (short)
- Trigger: alert CALIBRATION_DRIFT_HIGH fires.
- Initial responder: applied-ml oncall (pager).
- Actions:
  1) Triage alert dashboard; confirm which slice(s) exceeded threshold.
  2) Pull recent anchors and run fit-calibration locally; note deltas in ECE.
  3) If automated transform candidate passes gates, open rollout ticket and follow Rollout policy.
  4) If anchors show ASI < 0.9, pause automated relabeling and open annotation audit.
  5) Document actions and mark incident for postmortem if remediation > 12h.

Governance and ownership
- Applied-ML team: maintain calibration code and transform registry.
- Annotation team: maintain anchor registry and adjudication process.
- Observability: provide dashboards and daily health checks.
- Security: review anchor exports for PII; exports must be scrubbed per data-management policy.

Appendix: audit table (example columns)
- response_id | model_version | raw_score | calibrated_score | anchor_id | label_before | label_after | annotators | adjudicator | audit_reason | timestamp

Notes and caveats
- Calibration on synthetic/staged traffic may not generalize to production customer prompts — always validate on production-sampled anchors.
- For heavy-tailed score distributions, consider stratified isotonic fits to avoid overfitting high-score regions.
- Changes to scoring that affect user-facing behavior must coordinate with Product (change advisory).
